Subject: Re: Draft DPA - BrightBank redlines (round 1)

Emma — thanks for the redline. I pulled the file and annotated our positions; please find the summary below and see the attached PDF for inline comments.

Summary of RIF legal positions (round 1):
- Transfers: We are willing to adopt the EU SCCs (controller-processor) for EU personal data transfers; we will also sign a standard EU Addendum rather than unilateral language. We cannot accept an open-ended transfer restriction that prevents routing to our dedicated hosts in US regions; proposed compromise language in attached PDF.
- Subprocessors: We will provide a current subprocessor inventory and a 30-day notification process for material changes. We decline unilateral approval rights; offer a right to object within 10 business days with escalation path.
- Incident notification: We can commit to notifying within 72 hours of becoming aware of a security incident that impacts personal data; we request narrow scope and a mutual cooperation clause.
- Audit & access: We do not accept unlimited audit rights; propose SOC2 report delivery, onsite audit only for material breach with reasonable notice and cost allocation.
- Liability: We propose a mutual liability cap equal to the greater of USD $2,000,000 or 12 months of fees for breach of security/privacy obligations. Carveouts for willful misconduct and indemnity remain.
- Retention: We accept retention limits tied to the customer contract and will delete or return data within 60 days of termination unless retention is required by law.

Attached: RIF_DPA_Response_annotated.pdf (inline comments + suggested language)

DocuSign plan suggestion: prepare two envelopes — one for the DPA (legal signatories) and one for the SOW/PO (commercial). We can pre-populate the envelope with the HubSpot deal ID and a field for PO number. Let us know if BrightBank requires combined execution.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
